routes.description: Establish that transcendental facts require an adequate metaphysical ground and that a necessary personal mind explains their character and rational applicability better than the available non-theistic alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the need for grounding is established, impersonal and naturalistic accounts are comparatively inadequate, a necessary personal mind provides the relevant explanation, and philosophical or abductive support qualifies as good evidence for that conclusion.

motionBridge.description: Show that transcendental facts make a necessary personal God sufficiently better supported to constitute good evidence for the motion.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the necessity, objectivity, and applicability of transcendental facts call for an explanation beyond their practical use or description.
Connect the abstract and necessary character of transcendental facts to a necessary transcendent mind capable of grounding them.
Show that the divine account has greater explanatory adequacy than naturalism, Platonism, brute fact, or unspecified alternatives.
Establish that deductive and abductive philosophical reasoning can warrant the grounding inference without requiring exclusively empirical confirmation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how a unified necessary ground can satisfy parsimony and explanatory-scope requirements.
Specify what kind of non-theistic alternative or evidentiary objection would materially defeat the proposed explanation.

routes.description: Show that transcendental facts can be accepted without a demonstrated personal ground and that the proposed divine explanation fails to discriminate among alternatives or meet an adequate public evidentiary standard.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if grounding is not shown necessary, the inference from transcendental facts to a personal God remains underdetermined, and the available observations do not provide sufficiently specific, reliable, or comparative support for the divine hypothesis.

motionBridge.description: Show that transcendental facts do not provide sufficiently discriminating support for a necessary personal God to count as good evidence.

centralBridges.description: Establish that logical truths may hold or describe reality without a further personal or transcendent ontological ground.
Show that consistency with transcendental facts does not establish God as more likely than unexamined or non-theistic alternatives.
Require support that reliably connects the observed facts to a sufficiently specific divine hypothesis and establishes the argument's premises.
Compare the ambiguity and limited public verifiability of the evidence with what a capable personal God could be expected to provide.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why withholding judgment can avoid adding an unevidenced entity when the need for an additional ground is disputed.
Distinguish possible first-person warrant from evidence capable of supporting the divine conclusion for other people.

sections.title: Whether Transcendental Facts Require a Ground
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether the explanatory demand initiating the transcendental argument is warranted or whether logical necessity and practical reliability can stand without an additional metaphysical foundation.

sections.title: From Transcendental Facts to a Necessary Personal Mind
sections.rationale: This section covers the indispensable inferential step from the properties of logic and other abstract truths to mind, personality, necessity, and ultimately the specific kind of God asserted by the motion.

sections.title: Abduction, Alternatives, and Comparative Explanation
sections.rationale: The motion depends on whether the divine account can be compared responsibly with naturalism, Platonism, brute facts, agnosticism, and unspecified alternatives under explanatory-scope and parsimony criteria.

sections.title: Standards for Good Evidence and Sound Inference
sections.rationale: The parties dispute whether philosophical and abductive support can establish the relevant premises or whether reliable, specific, testable, and publicly confirmable support is required for the God hypothesis.

sections.title: Divine Revelation, Hiddenness, and Evidential Expectations
sections.rationale: Claims about what a capable personal God could reveal bear on whether ambiguous transcendental and cumulative evidence fits the hypothesis and on the distinction between private warrant and public support.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: The objective, necessary, timeless, immaterial, and transcendent character of logical laws is better grounded in a transcendent personal mind than in naturalism or abstract Platonism.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Appealing to brute facts or an unknown ground does not remove the explanatory demand, while God is proposed as a self-existing necessary fact rather than an unexplained contingent posit.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: One divine ground offers a unified explanation of transcendental facts with parsimony, coherence, explanatory power, and explanatory scope rather than multiplying brute or separate explanations.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Because naturalism allegedly cannot ground transcendental facts and abstract truths are intelligible as mental concepts, those truths are more coherently grounded in a mind.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Deductive implication and abductive defense of premises can support a sound philosophical argument, and restricting evidence to direct empirical repeatability imposes a self-undermining standard.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: A demand for an incontrovertible link to God becomes unattainable when naturalistic, brute-fact, or skeptical alternatives are always permitted regardless of the observation offered.

chunk-004:c004-08.proposition: Merely suggesting that some unspecified alternative explanation might exist does not defeat an abductive case unless a substantive competing explanation or objection is supplied.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: Agreement that transcendental facts function reliably does not answer the distinct meta-level question of what explains or grounds those facts.

chunk-005:chunk005-c03.proposition: God is not hidden because creation, morality, transcendental facts, special revelation, Jesus, and the resurrection collectively constitute publicly available evidence.

chunk-005:chunk005-c06.proposition: Universal revelation can place people under an obligation to know God without implying that God intends to compel every person to acquire settled belief.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: Good evidence for God should reduce bias and reliably support a sufficiently specific, testable hypothesis through such features as repeatability, independent verification, falsifiability, and causal relevance.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Abductive selection is unreliable when the candidate set is incomplete, because compatibility with observations does not establish that an extraordinary hypothesis is the most likely explanation.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: A vague classical-theist mind or creator cannot function as a discrete hypothesis, so unexplained logic or order does not warrant an inference to the necessary personal God asserted by the motion.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: An abductive supernatural conclusion lacks warrant without a near-exhaustive candidate set, comparative likelihood data, and confirmed instances of divine causation, and cannot follow merely from the absence of a natural explanation.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Persistent obscurity and disagreement about unfalsifiable God claims conflict with the clear evidence reasonably expected if a capable classical-theist God wanted its existence known.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: The basic laws of logic appear necessarily true whether or not God exists, and no transcendent realm or personal foundation has been demonstrated as necessary for their truth.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Logical and mathematical laws can describe reality through identity and noncontradiction without requiring an additional entity or foundation to guarantee that their relations hold.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: A valid argument is not good evidence for God unless its premises are demonstrated true, because the debated conclusion requires soundness rather than formal validity alone.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Even an extraordinary celestial message could be evidence toward a god without establishing Yahweh or another specific personal deity, particularly while rival explanations remain and direct divine communication is absent.

chunk-005:chunk005-c05.proposition: If God wants everyone to know that God exists and has an effective means of ensuring that knowledge but does not use it, observed nonbelief counts against attributing that desire to God.
